title: Sound engine, music and room music
divergences: Not compared with hardware or an emulator. MidiKey2Freq (BIOS) uses the high-level formula; the PSG and the output mixer are an emulation of the GBA sound hardware, resampled to 48 kHz with a zero-order hold of the FIFO that keeps the held sample across GBA frames (the port once reset it to zero at each frame's start, a 60 Hz buzz) and PSG steps that carry their fractional cycles; the sound device pulls the output (SDL's stream callback): each pull runs UpdateAudio and renders one GBA frame (280896 cycles) at a time at the 65.536 kHz PWM rate that MZM selects in SOUNDBIAS, and SDL's band-limited resampler converts it for the device; the game only changes the engine's state under the stream's lock, so a slow game frame can no longer starve the device (the earlier push from the game steps ran the queue dry and crackled), and the music keeps the hardware's 59.73 Hz frame clock independently of the game's speed; REG_VCOUNT reads as 160 during UpdateAudio. The room's track is chosen when the destination room is loaded (natively when the door is touched) and starts when the door fade ends; the alarm, Norfair and cutscene music cases (unk_378c, unk_38d8, the gMusicTrackInfo.unk checks). The 7-entry channel backups drop what would overflow them instead of writing past the array. A zero divisor in unk_1ccc is taken as a zero quotient.
notes: The custom C engine is ported routine by routine with the assembly mixer: the sequencer commands, DirectSound channels with the native envelope, allocation and group-of-four mixing paths, the four PSG channels through their registers, reverb, fades and the sound queue. ROM data (songs, voice groups, samples) is read through its GBA addresses from a private sound bank; out-of-table ROM reads of GetNoteDelay and unk_1ccc are exported. Rooms export their musicTrack and the runtime plays it through CheckSetNewMusicTrack and CheckPlayTransitionMusicTrack; the gameplay modules request their sound effects through mzm_sfx (identifiers generated from the decompilation's Sound enum by scripts/mzm_sound_ids.py), which the runtime forwards to the engine. InsertMusicAndQueueCurrent saves the channels of players 1, 3, 6 and 8 (unk_34ac), stops the others and plays the inserted music on player 0; its 0xB6 end runs ReplayQueuedMusic, which restores them (unk_35d0) and restarts the current music. BackupTrackData2SoundChannels / RetrieveTrackData2SoundChannels release and restore the channels of player 2; mzm_sfx carries PlayMusic, UpdateMusicPriority, FadeMusic, the insertion and the backup requests. With the extracted bank the item jingle plays 355 frames before Brinstar resumes (an engine-only check: captures have no sound). The pause lowers the music (DecreaseMusicVolume: the pause sound, the other players' channels saved, unk_3058 with gUnk_Audio0x50 on players 0 and 1, kept by ReplayQueuedMusic) and ResetMusicVolume restores it when the pause screen closes. DecreaseMusicVolume (the pause) plays SOUND_63 (0x63); the port once queued sound 63 (MUSIC_IMAGO_COCOON_BATTLE), which replaced the room's music after the pause. Rendering the extracted Brinstar music offline confirmed the fix: the per-frame spike of the output's second difference fell from about ten times its mean to the level of the FIFO's own steps; what remains (the envelopes applied once a frame) is already in the mixer's output.
next_action: Trigger the sounds of the systems still to port (charge beam, bombs, liquids, ground effects, bosses); compare a rendered track with an emulator capture.

Checked by capture in crateria_016 with --event 16 (the pillar rising, then the platforms appearing). Gerons in their idle state catch every Parasite whose point is inside them (the Parasite's collision cleared so it counts once); four destroy them; checked by capture in brinstar_023 (VARIA3 destroyed, VARIA1 getting destroyed).

title: Save platforms (and the Chozodia save platform)
divergences: Not compared with an emulator. The parts keep the sprites' priority and the OBJ blending of the tube is not drawn. The Chozodia platform's alarm transparency (BLDCNT/BLDALPHA) is not modelled, and its off palette row 3 reads another graphics slot's palette and is not baked (it draws with its own row).
notes: The AIs follow the decompilation: the platform (always active, its top part eight blocks above) opens after Samus stands on it for 10 frames (not crouching or morphed), and once opened grabs her (centred, invincibility cleared, SPOSE_TURNING_FROM_FACING_THE_FOREGROUND with her animation frozen, gDisablePause), spawns the save prompt after 4 frames, and on YES flashes with palette row 2 (a baked /row2 variant) while the top extends and the tube, its shadow and the rising ray play; the ray turns it off, the save complete message follows a second later, then a 10-frame delay and the release (SPOSE_FACING_THE_FOREGROUND, the pause allowed again); Samus walking off closes it. In a loaded file's room (gIsLoadingFile) it starts with the tube around Samus and releases her after 340 frames. Checked by capture in brinstar_033 (prompt, saving, message, release, reload). A new game is the native one whatever the runtime's test options: Sram_InitSaveFile and SamusInit without a file (99 energy, no item, no ammunition, no event, no collected item, no opened hatch, a zero timer, the chosen difficulty), the gunship landing in Crateria, the intro text, then RoomLoad at Brinstar's door 0 (x = xStart blocks + xExit + 8 pixels, y = yEnd + 1 blocks + yExit pixels - 1, its own exit exported as X lines) with SamusInit's pose facing the foreground, facing left; checked by a capture of the whole flow from the title screen (Samus at x 632, falling down the first shaft, 99 energy and no ammunition). The equipment is no longer rebuilt from the debug suit preset: the collected items stay through the debug menu, and Samus's graphics follow the equipment. The Chozodia save platform (PSPRITE_SAVE_PLATFORM_CHOZODIA, its own tables, part and sounds, the off tables swapped, off during the alarm) refills Samus before the prompt: energy, then missiles, super missiles and power bombs (energy only suitless) with each counter's refill animation, the refill light and sound, then MESSAGE_WEAPONS_AND_ENERGY_RESTORED (MESSAGE_ENERGY_TANK_RECHARGE_COMPLETE suitless); checked by capture in chozodia_004 (30 energy refilled, the message, the save written, the file loaded back into the tube and Samus released). Both variants initialize off while EscapeDetermineTimer reports the Tourian or Chozodia escape.
next_action: Compare both platforms with an emulator; port the escape that switches them off.

title: Escape countdown and Zebes destruction
divergences: All twelve Tourian escape stages and their post-cutscene handoff are connected. The first stage's room views still omit their native block-layer tilemaps, although their explosion/debris OAM and camera shake are present. The explosion actor is stored outside gSpriteData, so its RNG omits the native free sprite slot. Both gameplay fade transitions use one host white overlay rather than applying brightness separately to selected GBA palette rows; the exit background effect therefore also whitens Samus before the global fade. The native suitless item-acquisition map sequence is not ported: the post-Tourian monologue enters Chozodia room 0 directly; the paralyzer pistol is covered by mzm.weapons.paralyzer_pistol.
notes: Mother Brain's death starts the invisible Zebes explosion actor at its native offset. It follows the native 16-frame particle and debris cadence, camera-relative positions, Samus-height correction, four explosion sounds and ten-frame two-axis shakes. When the Zebes escape banner finishes spawning, EscapeStart and EscapeSetTimer select the event-driven escape and difficulty duration (easy 3:00, normal 2:00, hard 1:00); the native hundredths and seconds cadence freezes outside gameplay or while movement is prevented. ParticleEscape copies both rows of sEscapeTimerDigitsGfx to their native OBJ VRAM addresses and draws the eight 8x16 OAM objects at their absolute HUD position. At zero, the runtime freezes Samus and the countdown, fades all sounds and music over 60 frames, applies ColorFadingProcess_EscapeFailed's eight white levels, holds white for 61 frames, then enters the native Game Over screen. A successful gunship take-off applies the native exit fades and enters GM_TOURIAN_ESCAPE. TourianEscapeInit loads the native room, OBJ graphics and palettes. TourianEscapeZebesExploding switches from Tourian room 4 to Tourian room 5 and Crateria room 1 at frames 104 and 176, animates four native explosion objects and five debris objects with the room shake, starts the cutscene music, then shows Zebes with the animated departing ship and scrolling explosion through frame 512. TourianEscapeSamusInHerShip runs through frame 372: it selects the Power or Varia palette, expands the native brightness window around suited Samus, reveals the suitless image with the three removal sounds, alpha-fades the flash, and switches to her opened eyes. TourianEscapeSamusLookingAround runs for 57 frames: its two alpha-blended OAM halves converge vertically on the centre of the cockpit while BG0 switches from the left to the right native tilemap. TourianEscapeSamusSurrounded runs for 113 frames: a fixed BG0 cockpit surrounds a centred affine BG2 view that zooms out from Samus's ship to reveal the pirate formation between frames 32 and 47. TourianEscapeSamusFlyingIn reuses the intro starfield, ship graphics and complex affine OAM for 33 frames: the two six/nine-part ship poses alternate as its vertical speed eases and its scale rises from 32 to 480. TourianEscapeSamusChasedByPirates runs for 257 frames: six alternating particles recycle across the scrolling starfield while Samus and three pirate ships cross in both directions with their native OAM poses, coordinates and four sound cues. TourianEscapeSamusChasedByPiratesFiring runs for 385 frames: inherited projectiles rise and recycle while Samus follows eight native accelerated paths, both formations use complex affine OAM, the pirate group shrinks away and three sound cues cover the firing, dodging and departure. TourianEscapeSamusGettingShot runs for 401 frames: a brightness fade reveals Samus and six inherited projectiles over the scrolling starfield, the ship decelerates then oscillates after the hit, and the decisive shot switches to the dedicated BG1 view and sound. TourianEscapeSamusGoingToCrash runs for 81 frames: the damaged ship and its two looping smoke trails are alpha-blended over Zebes, while their native OAM offsets and alternating fire palette accompany a six-frame background drift and the free-falling sound. TourianEscapeSamusCrashing runs for 289 frames: the falling ship crosses a foreground view with four debris poses, the collision reveals the explosion layer and raises every layer to full white before the long native hold. TourianEscapeSamusLookingAtSky runs for 433 frames: the crash white reveals three native layers, two pirate ships cross diagonally, the layers pan at their independent thresholds and the scene ends on black. TourianEscapeSamusLookingAtMotherShip runs its two drifting native backgrounds under diagonal rain, renders ""The timing..."" into OBJ VRAM, alpha-fades its twelve-part text composition over the image, darkens the view and holds frame 448 until A or B. The following frame starts CUTSCENE_COULD_I_SURVIVE; dismissing it activates suitless Samus and loads Chozodia room 0. The --tourian-escape runtime option exposes the sequence for direct captures. The same timer core includes Mecha Ridley's 5:00 or hard 3:00 route. Save platforms initialize in their native off state while either escape is active.
next_action: Port the suitless item-acquisition map sequence; separately supply the first scene's room block tilemaps.

title: Keyboard and gamepad input
divergences: Host input layer: SDL3 devices are mapped to the GBA KEYINPUT bits; the native key reading and repeat logic are not ported.
notes: Hot-plugged SDL3 gamepads, a remappable GBA layout and the keyboard drive Samus; no in-game controls menu yet.
next_action: Port the native input routines and add an in-game controls menu.

title: Area and room name banners
divergences: The location texts are baked in the banner's graphics by the exporter (English only), as /ltN library variants; the banner always draws as graphics slot 7 (its slot of the spriteset only matters for the palette rows, which are baked). gLastDoorUsed is known for door transitions and the new game's start (door 0); a loaded file shows only the save and map room banners of their spritesets. The banner is drawn after the front backgrounds (BG priority 0) at its GBA screen position, the GBA screen centred in the wider view. Not compared with an emulator.
notes: SpriteUtilInitLocationText: when a room is entered through a door flagged DOOR_TYPE_DISPLAYS_ROOM_LOCATION (exported as Y lines) the area's location text (LocationTextGet*: BRINSTAR, KRAID, NORFAIR, RIDLEY, TOURIAN, CRATERIA, CHOZODIA, MOTHERSHIP, PLANET ZEBES, CHOZO RUINS, the map rooms...), and in a save or map room spriteset always its name, put an area banner in sprite slot 0 at an absolute screen position: an area's name scrolls in at the bottom for 2 seconds (sAreaBannerLocationTextPal), a room's name in the middle for 1.5 seconds (5/6 of a second for the save and map rooms, none of those while the alarm rings), then scrolls out. TextDrawLocation's text (mask mode over 0xFF, its two tile rows copied to the graphics slot) is drawn by the exporter with the native font. Checked by capture: BRINSTAR at a new game's start and SAVE ROOM in brinstar_033. The tests run both banners and the alarm case.
next_action: Port the falling Chozo pillar with the Ruins Test, then compare with an emulator.

title: HUD and minimap
divergences: Not compared with hardware or an emulator. The runtime view is 320x224, wider than the GBA screen: the HUD keeps its native positions from the view's top-left corner and the minimap is placed 26 pixels from the view's right edge (SCREEN_SIZE_X replaced by the view width). Only the HUD is drawn by the PPU (its OAM slots; the other sprites keep the runtime's own drawing), so the HUD is always in front. Without a save system the minimap progress (gVisitedMinimapTiles, gMinimapTilesWithObtainedItems, downloaded maps) lasts one session; the Hiragana tiles, the debug room info and the boss icon updates by Kraid, Ridley and the ship (MinimapUpdateChunk has no caller yet) are not wired.
notes: HudDraw runs after ProjectileUpdate every frame and writes the native OBJ VRAM and OAM of a GbaPpu: sCommonSpritesGfx at VRAM_OBJ + 0x800 and sCommonSpritesPal at OBJ palette rows 2 to 7 (the in-game init), the energy digits and the energy tank row (sEnergyTanksGfx_* by full tanks, the low health flag under 30), the three refill animation stages of the energy, missile, super missile and power bomb counters (gEnergyRefillAnimation and the others, set by the Chozo statue refills), the missile, super missile and power bomb counters composed from 4-pixel digits (sMissileDigitsGfx, sPowerBombDigitsGfx) with their Inactive, Selected or Active symbol (HudUpdateGfx follows gSamusWeaponInfo.weaponHighlighted and missilesSelected), the suitless charge bar, the native escape countdown objects, and the OAM entries of HudUpdateOam (health bar, counters only when their maximum is non-zero, the minimap and its square blinking every 8 frames). The minimap decompresses the area's sMinimapDataPointers map (LZ77), adds the obtained items, hides the unexplored tiles unless the map is downloaded (MinimapSetDownloadedTiles), follows Samus's screen (MinimapCheckForUnexploredTile with the room entry's mapX and mapY read from sAreaRoomEntryPointers), marks it explored, records the area names, and redraws one 3-tile line a frame through the sPauseScreen_40d74c / _40d6fc color tables with the four flips. Checked in brinstar_000 (`--spawn 212 496`): energy 99, missiles, super missiles and power bombs with their symbols, the minimap with the Morph Ball room tile and the blinking square.
next_action: Port the pause screen map and status screen on the same PPU, then save the minimap progress.

title: Message banner and its text
divergences: The banner is kept outside the sprite slots and is drawn centred in the wider runtime view (the GBA position 120, 54 offset by the view's extra 32 rows); it always loads its graphics (no spriteset holds it); the item acquisition pause screen is not ported; the English text is the only language exported.
notes: The exporter transliterates TextProcessMessageBanner, TextProcessCurrentMessage and TextDrawMessageCharacter on the banner's OBJ VRAM (sMessageBannerGfx, color 15 fill, glyphs of sCharactersGfx with sCharacterWidths, eight characters a frame, the US line overflow) for every English message of sMessageTextPointers, renders the banner's six OAM tables with each message, and records the TextProcessMessageBanner calls each message takes. The runtime runs MessageBanner frame by frame: the nine graphics frames, the text processing with the animation held, the shown banner (items and first tanks back up player 2 and insert the item or unknown item jingle; the fully powered suit plays the Brinstar remix behind its jingle; tank messages back up player 2, play the tank jingle and retrieve player 2 at removal; maps and save complete play the tank jingle; one-line tables for items, first tanks, maps, save complete and the fully powered suit), 100 static frames before A, B or a direction closes it, the removal animation, gPreventMovementTimer held at SAMUS_ITEM_PMT meanwhile (SamusUpdate skipped, sprites stopped except uninitialized ones, no Samus contact); its removal finishes a tank collection, and the end of an item message's text (stage 3 of the text processing) runs BgClipFinishCollectingAbility, which registers the ability in gItemsCollected and on the minimap. Once removed, the banner keeps its last pose, as its sprite slot does natively, for the map station that waits for MESSAGE_BANNER_POSE_REMOVAL_ANIMATION. The save prompt spawns its YES/NO cursor (SaveYesNoCursor, drawn at its absolute position shifted like the banner): LEFT and RIGHT move it with their sound, A answers (work1), NO plays the refusal and closes the banner, YES hides the cursor and saves on its next update (MZM_BANNER_SAVE); the save complete message re-enables the pause when it goes. The Zebes and Chozodia escape messages emit EscapeStart when their spawning animation reaches its static table.
next_action: Port the item acquisition screen.

title: Item, hint and unknown item Chozo statues, refills and hints
divergences: The background flashes (MakeBackgroundFlash), gSlowScrollingTimer and gDisablePause are not ported (the hint map screen is, mzm.menus.pause_map_screen); the HUD refill animations are counters only; the unknown items are kept obtained but inactive with no way to activate them yet (the fully powered suit and its status screen are not ported); SP_SOLID_FOR_PROJECTILES is not modelled (the statue's hitbox is empty).
notes: The eight item statues (Long, Ice and Wave Beams, Bombs, Speed Booster, High Jump, Screw Attack, Varia Suit) and their hint statues run ChozoStatue with gSubSpriteData1: the multi-sprite tables (Standing, Sitting, Seated) are read from the decompilation, the head and leg take their OAM and position from it, the eye, arm and glow parts their position; the statue faces its native direction, makes its seated or standing body solid (CAA_MAKE_NON_POWER_GRIP, the hint statue's hand CAA_MAKE_SOLID_GRIPPABLE) and spawns its parts and, while Samus lacks the item, the ball. The ball (SSC_SOLID, one health) reveals the item when shot, then Samus touching it starts gPreventMovementTimer, registers the item and its events (ChozoStatueRegisterItem) and opens the item's one-line message banner, the ball flickering until the banner closes; the statue then waits 40 frames and idles, its arm glowing. Statues draw with their own graphics; the sprite engine gained drawOrder, SP_ALWAYS_ACTIVE and graphics owners for secondary sprites. Checked in brinstar_005: shooting the ball reveals the Long Beam orb, touching it shows the "Long Beam" banner, and after A the ball is gone and the hand glows. The statue's hand grabs Samus (SPOSE_GRABBED_BY_CHOZO_STATUE, at its exact height and within a quarter block): a hint statue in the Morph Ball or rolling registers the hint, opens its eye, fades the music for a second (FadeMusic), flashes its palette rows (sChozoStatueFlashingPaletteRows every 12 frames, the hint sound), plays MUSIC_CHOZO_STATUE_HINT, sits down along the Sitting table with flickering echoes (SpawnChozoStatueMovement), seats and refills; a refill statue in the Morph Ball refills energy, missiles, super missiles and power bombs (SpriteUtilRefill*, each followed by 13 frames of its HUD counter) with the refill glow and palette flash, opens "Energy Tank recharge complete" or "Weapons and energy fully restored", sleeps, closes its eye (a hint statue then replays gMusicTrackInfo.currentRoomTrack, the last room track the runtime entered) and lets Samus go when she may move. The exporter adds the statues' palette rows 1 to 3. Checked in brinstar_005 (`--spawn 126 112 --item long-beam`, Down twice): grabbed, golden flash, refill banner, released in the hand; in brinstar_002 (`--spawn 808 112`, Down twice) the Long Beam hint statue grabs Samus, flashes, sits down with her and refills. The unknown item statues (Plasma Beam, Space Jump, Gravity Suit) run the same AI with their own OAM tables (UnknownItemChozoStatue*, the unknown balls), multi-sprite tables (read from the positional initializers of the decompilation), part and refill sprites; their item is obtained (gEquipment.beamBombs / suitMisc) but stays inactive, as UpdateSuitType keeps it for the normal suit, and its banner reads "Unknown Item". Checked in kraid_033 (`--spawn 186 128`, B, Right): the Space Jump statue's ball reveals the unknown orb and touching it shows "Unknown Item". A hint statue's flashing ends by opening the hint map screen (gPauseScreenFlag PAUSE_SCREEN_CHOZO_HINT) with the hint music, then the statue sits down.
next_action: Port the background flashes and the slow scrolling, then the fully powered suit's unknown item activation.

title: Enemy drops
divergences: The grouped energy drop has no natural in-game source until Mecha Ridley is ported; the drop behavior has not been compared with an emulator.
notes: Drop rolls from the ROM probabilities (as the sprite or, for respawning sprites, as a drop following its slot) with the full energy and ammunition substitutions, the hidden spawn, pickup refills, blinking and despawn timers, native BG1 priority, and the common sprite graphics are ported. Power bomb drops spawn and refill one power bomb with their sound. Mecha Ridley's grouped pickup selects one of three native OAM tables from its follower slot, refills 60 energy and clamps to maximum.
next_action: Port Mecha Ridley so its grouped energy drops become reachable in normal play, then compare their presentation with an emulator.

title: Morph Ball, Power Grip and Charge Beam pickups
divergences: the flicker timers never move, as in the game.
notes: The Morph Ball (outline sprite with the ball's status), the Power Grip (glow removed once it is taken, EVENT_POWER_GRIP_OBTAINED) and the Charge Beam (spawning table, glow following its height, the float of sChargeBeamIdleYMovement, EVENT_CHARGE_BEAM_OBTAINED): removed when owned, touched they give their item, hold Samus with SAMUS_ITEM_PMT and the item banner with its jingle, and flicker until the banner releases her. Checked in brinstar_000 (--spawn 212 496: the jump onto the pillar takes the Morph Ball and shows its banner) and crateria_012 ( the Power Grip from the statue's hands).
next_action: Compare with the original game frame by frame.

title: Energy, missile, super missile and power bomb tanks
divergences: the transition probes run every frame for doors, the tank probes on odd frames only.
notes: On odd frames, the four probes of BgClipCheckTouchingTransitionOrTank (Samus's right and left hitbox edges on her center row, the bottom and top rows on her center column) read the behaviors of the current Clipdata, last probe first; a revealed tank (hidden ones are not tanks until their block breaks) on an explored minimap tile (MinimapCheckIsTileExplored) starts gCollectingTank, sets gPreventMovementTimer, raises the equipment within the game total (sStartingHealthAmmo, the total of sNumberOfTanksPerArea and sTankIncreaseAmount, exported from the decompilation: 100 energy refilled, 5 missiles, 2 super missiles, 2 power bombs) and spawns the message banner (the first missile, super missile or power bomb tank with its own message). BgClipFinishCollectingTank (on the banner's removal) empties the BG1 block, clears the Clipdata to air or water (underwater tanks) and registers the item in gItemsCollected by area and room and on the minimap (MinimapUpdateForCollectedItem); BgClipRemoveCollectedTanks removes them again on every room load. Checked in brinstar_019 (`--spawn 615 96`, Right): Samus walks onto the energy tank column, energy 99 to 199, the banner shows its two lines and Samus stays frozen until A; the tank block is then empty. The tank increases follow the game's difficulty (sTankIncreaseAmount[gDifficulty]: 100/5/2/2 on easy and normal, 50/2/1/1 on hard), exported per difficulty.
next_action: Save the collected items and the minimap progress with a save file.

title: Pause easy sleep
divergences: The Stop syscall (SYSCALL 3 with the keypad interrupt on SELECT, L and R) is reproduced as a sleeping state: the runtime stops presenting the screen (black, the LCD being off) and pauses the audio device instead of SoundBias0; the game keeps polling the keys each frame. gDisableSoftReset is not modeled (no soft reset exists). The English text is always used. Not compared with an emulator.
notes: L on the map screen plays the opening sound and runs PauseScreenEasySleepInit: the map fades out by four BLDALPHA levels a frame, the L prompt and the visor overlays change, the easy sleep tilemap replaces the map overlay and the equipment names graphics are backed up and replaced by the text, drawn a few steps a frame in the mask mode (TextDrawEasySleep with TextProcessCurrentMessage and TextDrawMessageCharacter: "Activate Easy Sleep?" and the SELECT, L and R hint, plus the YES/NO prompt drawn by TextDrawYesNoEasySleep at PauseScreenInit), then it fades in with the cursor on NO. LEFT and RIGHT move the cursor with their sound, A on NO refuses, B, L or R closes (PauseScreenQuitEasySleep restores the overlay and the graphics); A on YES waits half a second, blanks the screen and sleeps until SELECT, L and R are held, then waits for every key to be released with the cursor back on NO. Checked by capture in brinstar_000.
next_action: Compare the screen and the timings with an emulator.

title: File select screen
divergences: The corrupted file handling, the options (stereo, sound test, gallery, time attack records, Fusion link, NES Metroid) and the time attack code are not ported: the options entry is shown but A on it does nothing. The Japanese text menu is skipped as in the US version. A new game plays the gunship's landing in Crateria (mzm.environment.gunship) and the intro text cutscene (mzm.cutscenes.story_text), then starts in the runtime's first room. FileSelectCopyFileHandler is ported from its NON_MATCHING C version. The text buffers' fills follow the US binary, which adds their offsets in bytes where the decompiled source's u32 pointers would scale them (checked in the disassembly of mzm_us.elf). Not compared with an emulator.
notes: START on the title enters the US file select screen on the native screen PPU: the Chozo background, the menu and panel tilemaps from the ROM bank, the three files with their energy and tanks (HudDrawEnergy into the file's tiles), timer or dashes, difficulty and area, the Metroid logos of completed files, the music, and the fade in. UP and DOWN move between the files and the enabled entries (with the maintained input repeat) with the file markers and Samus's head cursor; B fades out to the intro (GM_INTRO). A on a file opens its "Start game" panel (the window, the alpha fade and the BG2 scroll), whose text is drawn line by line with the native font; A there continues a saved file (the start animation, then the save is loaded), or on a completed file offers continue / new game / time attack and the overwrite confirmation, and on a new file opens the difficulty panel (hard once unlocked, completed difficulties highlighted) before the start; B closes the panels back. Checked by capture: the files, the panels, a new game and a continued file. Copy (with at least one file) chooses a source among the used files (a time attack file is refused with its message) and a destination among the other files (the first empty one, else A/B), shown by the green markers and the arrow, confirms the overwrite of a used destination, copies the file (SramCopyFile) and redraws it; erase chooses a used file, confirms it (NO by default) and deletes it (SramDeleteFile) before redrawing; B leaves each step. The runtime copies and deletes the save files themselves.
next_action: Port the options screen (stereo, sound test), then compare the screen with an emulator.

title: Pause screen map download
divergences: BG1 and BG2 show screens 24 and 23, which this mode never loads: the game's leftover VRAM there is not kept (the screen PPU is cleared). The game's fade into the pause is not played and the music is not lowered (as in the game, only START lowers it). The HUD minimap is redrawn and transferred over the next frames instead of the HUD graphics reload of the return to the game. The unused instant download types 1 and 2 are not ported. Not compared with an emulator.
notes: With PAUSE_SCREEN_MAP_DOWNLOAD, PauseScreenInit flags the screen as on the map and downloading, keeps the explored map on BG3, marks the area's map downloaded, recomputes gDecompressedMinimapVisitedTiles with the downloaded tiles (PauseScreenGetMinimapData, MinimapSetDownloadedTiles), uses the download BG layout (the visor on BG0 at the highest priority, BG3 with the mosaic bit, BG1 scrolled by 4 pixels), shows only the area name (priority 0), Samus's and the boss icons at priority 1 (the boss icon hidden until the line passes it) and no scroll arrows or viewable areas. PauseScreenMapDownload waits 8 frames, starts the line from the BG3 scroll, copies one map row every 8 frames for 21 rows while the line and its four trails move, transfers the whole map, redraws the minimap, removes the line and waits half a second; then A, B or START leaves. Checked by capture in brinstar_032.
next_action: Compare the screen with an emulator, then port the Chozo hint screen.

title: Pause screen map
divergences: The pause from the game, the map download and the Chozo statue hints are ported: the item acquisition and suit screens, the debug menu and the completion info and its tank counts (shown only after the game is completed) are not. The hint screen skips StatusScreenDraw and TextDrawYesNoEasySleep (their EWRAM tilemaps are never shown there); the boss flames' up and down movement (PauseScreenUpdateBossFlameAnimation) is never started by the game and is not ported. The game's fades around the pause (COLOR_FADING_CANCEL) darken Samus's and the HUD's frames by colour modulation; the room is not reloaded after the pause (the game keeps its state). Not compared with an emulator.
notes: START in the game (when movement is not prevented and no power bomb is out) lowers the music and opens the pause screen on the native screen's PPU: PauseScreenInit loads its palettes (sTankIconsPal, sMinimapTilesPal, sPauseScreen_3fcef0), graphics and tile maps (the minimap tiles, the visor overlays, the map and world map overlays, the area and menu names) from the ROM bank, puts the current area's explored map on BG3 (gDecompressedMinimapVisitedTiles) and every area's map (PauseScreenGetMinimapData with the obtained items, boss icons and the skipped Varia tile, then MinimapSetDownloadedTiles) in EWRAM, centres the view on Samus (PauseScreenMapSetSpawnPosition), sets the BG controls and alpha blending, and fades in by two color steps a frame. The map screen scrolls with the D-pad (CheckForMaintainedInput repeats), shows the scroll arrows, Samus's icon, the boss icon or its cross, the area name, animates the minimap palette, toggles the world map with A or B (its overlay, palette, area names and Samus's icon, with their sounds), switches between the viewable areas with SELECT (MapScreenChangeMap with sMapScreenAreasViewOrder) and opens the status screen with R (mzm.menus.status_screen) or easy sleep with L (mzm.menus.easy_sleep) and leaves with START or B: the fade out, then ResetMusicVolume and the game resumes. Checked by capture in brinstar_000 (pause, scroll, resume). The map stations open it in its map download mode (mzm.menus.map_download). Chozo statue hints (PAUSE_SCREEN_CHOZO_HINT): the hint screen (sChozoHintBackgroundGfx and its tile table, the area name, BG1's tint blended over the map), the statue's target found by its map position (sChozoStatueTargets), its icon travelling to the item (ChozoStatueHintMovement: the speed by distance, the trail every 8 frames) while the map scrolls to it (ChozoStatueHintScrolling), through the elevators to another area (sChozoStatueTargetPathPointers, sElevatorRoomPairs: the map fades out and in on the next area), then A or START fades the music (2 2/3 seconds) and leaves. The pause screen's map then shows the activated targets (the items still to collect after their hint, Kraid's and Ridley's flames), the elevators towards the first one and the world map's targets; the areas with a target become viewable. Checked by capture: the Long Beam hint in brinstar_002 (the statue's grab, the screen, the target and the scrolling, A, the statue sitting down) and the target on the pause map afterwards. The test runs that hint on the exported bank. ProcessPauseButtonPress: START (and a map station's or a hint statue's request) first fades the game to black in 8 frames (COLOR_FADING_CANCEL, every BG and OBJ row) while the sprites go on and Samus waits; the pause screen then opens, and on leaving it the game fades back in over 8 frames, Samus still waiting, before the pause's music volume is reset (UpdateMusicAfterPause). Checked by capture in brinstar_000.
next_action: Port the item acquisition screens, then compare with an emulator.

title: Pause status screen
divergences: Only the status screen of the normal pause is ported: the item acquisition, suitless and fully powered sequences (StatusScreenSuitlessItems, StatusScreenFullyPoweredItems, the unknown item palette, PauseScreenSuitChangingStart) and the debug status screen are not, so StatusScreenToggleItem only clears the SELECT prompt (the native toggling is disabled outside these sequences) and the suit change fade of the wireframe (PauseScreenFadeWireframeSamus) never starts. TextProcessDescription has no demo state. The English text pointers are always used. Not compared with an emulator.
notes: R on the map screen runs PauseScreenStatusScreenInit: the R prompt and its visor overlay, the opening sound, the map fades out through BLDALPHA (PauseScreenInitFading / PauseScreenApplyFading, two levels a frame), the status BG2 with its blend, the headers and Samus's wireframe (sSamusWireframeData, sSamusWireframePal by suit, an OBJ window copy showing only BG3 and the objects) slide in, fade in, become their linked versions, the equipment rows are revealed one a frame (StatusScreenDrawItems) and the cursor and text BG0 appear. PauseScreenInit draws the status tilemap from the runtime equipment (obtained and activated items, the plasma beam, gravity suit and space jump as unknown items before the fully powered suit, the bombs and missiles with their ammunition, the pistol when suitless) and the energy and ammunition amounts. The D-pad moves the item cursor between the enabled slots (StatusScreenGetDestinationSlot with the remembered left and right slots), each slot writes its description with the native font into the text tiles (TextProcessCurrentMessage, TextDrawCharacter with the ROM character widths and graphics), A skips the delay and turns the lines, and B, L or R goes back to the map (PauseScreenQuitStatusScreen). Checked by capture in brinstar_000 (long and charge beams, missiles, bombs, misc items).
next_action: Port the item acquisition and suit change sequences of the status screen with the item toggling, then compare the screen with an emulator.

title: Samus pose controller, physics and collisions
divergences: Not compared frame by frame with the original game. The liquid enter and exit effects (SamusUpdateEnvironmentalEffect) are not ported, and nothing enters the save, map download, zipline, escape ship or facing-the-background poses (their handlers are ported). The environmental effect sprites (gSamusEnvironmentalEffects) are not drawn, only their sounds play. The native probes allow transient overlaps (a spin broken under a low ceiling), which the tests accept for under a second.
notes: A transliteration of src/samus.c: the 67 poses of sSamusCollisionData with their hitboxes and standing statuses, every handler of sSamusPoseFunctionPointers and sSamusPoseGfxFunctionPointers, SamusSetPose with SamusSetMidAir, SamusSetLandingPose, the hurt and knockback poses and SamusCheckCarryFromCopy, SamusUpdatePhysics, the velocity update with DIV_SHIFT and the slope speeds, and the native point-probe collisions of SamusUpdateHitboxMovingDirection (the side, top, landing and ground probes, the corner nudges, slopes, the walk-off-ledge rule, the Power Grip ledge grab with the non power grip blocks). SamusAimCannon gives the running diagonals (Up or Down with the direction) and the no-aim run (ACD_NONE); the hanging poses turn to aim on Up, Down, L or the outward direction, climb after ten frames of Up without A, hide the arm cannon, pull into a morph ball tunnel under a block and shoot up or down. The animations time with sSamusAnimPointers_PowerSuit[pose] (or the suitless and the special tables) and the runtime draws the body animation of SamusUpdateGraphicsOam by its library key, whose arm cannon offsets place the shots (the Running [ACD_NONE - 2] rows are now exported); the shots take the offsets of the unarmed key, since the armed graphics variants have none and placed missiles at Samus's feet. The screw and speed booster block damage runs at the start of SamusCheckCollisions. Checked in brinstar_009 (--spawn 466 192: hanging, the Up+toward climb without A, a shot up from the hanging cannon) and brinstar_005 (a diagonal shot while running left). The hazards of ClipdataUpdateCurrentAffecting (the water, lava and acid blocks, and the room effect's hazard above or below its surface from the exported sHazeData) drive the liquid slowing of SamusUpdatePhysics (halved speeds and gravity, no Gravity Suit) and SamusTakeHazardDamage (the per-suit damage rates, the submerged sound, the cold knockback, the death). Checked in crateria_007: Samus runs at the slowed cap in the water. Elevator blocks work in the rooms of sElevatorRoomPairs (ClipdataCheckCantUseElevator, from the ROM bank; the second Crateria to Tourian route only after EVENT_ESCAPED_ZEBES): Up or Down on one turns Samus to the foreground, rides at the elevator speed with its sound, takes the area connection through BgClipCheckTouchingTransitionOnElevator and RoomLoad moves her three blocks on in the new room until the opposite elevator block stops her. Checked by capture: brinstar_026 to norfair_000. SamusDying's timer reaching 120 (after the animation's frame 23) flags the game over (gMainGameMode = GM_GAMEOVER). The shinespark and ballspark collisions start the shared screen shake (mzm_screen_shake), whose horizontal timer still drops Samus from a ledge.
next_action: Port the room effect wave, the liquid enter and exit effects, and the save platforms and map stations that enter their poses; compare with the original game frame by frame.

title: Speed booster, shinespark and ballspark
divergences: Liquids and the speed booster and shinespark aura sprites (gScrewSpeedAnimation) are not ported.
notes: With the Speed Booster, running above 96 subpixels a frame counts a timer to 160 (the cap rises to 140 at 120 and 160 at 140); from 160 subpixels a frame SamusCheckShinesparking starts the speed boost (sound, Running_Speedboosting, the speed boost palette rows by gFrameCounter8Bit % 6, the 160 ground and mid-air caps kept through jumps and the speed-boosted landing), cancelled below it and on death. Releasing the direction skids (10 subpixels a frame, the skidding sound); Down alone while skidding, or during the six frames after a speed-boosted roll in the Morph Ball, stores a shinespark for 180 frames (the palette and the charge sound every 16 frames). Speed boosting breaks speed blocks (DESTRUCTING_ACTION_SPEED and SPEED_ON_GROUND) and kills weak sprites as DCT_SPEEDBOOSTER with its particle and sound. Checked in tourian_010 with --item speed-booster: the speed boost palette and running animation after about 160 frames of running. With a stored shinespark, A (without a direction on the ground, with half a block of room, Samus rising by it) or A in the air starts the charge (50 frames of glow, the shinesparking sound, no gravity); when its animation ends the spark goes up by default at 192, sideways at 192 with the direction held, or diagonally (160, 96) with L or the direction and Up, through SamusSetPose with the speed boost on, killing weak sprites as DCT_SHINESPARK (its particle and sound). A ceiling or a wall ends it in the collision (48 frames of invincibility, the collision sound), 17 frames, then the delay after and a fall. In the Morph Ball with High Jump, A starts a ballspark: half a block up, a hop on the first frame, one second of charge with the ballsparking sound and the ball turning toward the input, then the same sparks, the collision and the Morph Ball fall. SamusSetPose stops the sounds when a charge or spark is cut short. Checked in tourian_010: run, skid, Down, A: the spark rises to the ceiling, then the delay after.
next_action: Port the aura sprites.

title: Room backgrounds: layers, priorities, animations, liquids, BG0 blend and BG3 scrolling
divergences: Each background is rendered alone by the PPU and the runtime composes them with its sprites by priority, so the BG0 blend is approximated by SDL blending (additive at EVA/16, alpha at 16 - EVB) instead of the GBA's per-pixel targets; the block layers are redrawn around the view every frame instead of the native row and column streaming (the same tiles); the mother ship common tiles (gUseMotherShipDoors, set by door types) are not tracked; the background effects (lightning, flashes), BG0 and BG3 movement (clouds, snow), the 0x43/0x44/dark-room BG0 positions, haze, gradients, windows and screen fades are not reproduced; without the ROM bank the exported metatile sheets are drawn instead (static). The camera is the runtime's 320x224 follow view.
notes: With the ROM bank, mzm_room_gfx rebuilds the room's VRAM and BG palettes as RoomLoadTileset leaves them (animated tiles at 0x4000, common tiles at 0x4800, the tileset at 0x5800, the BG3 graphics below 0xFDE0, palette rows 0-2 common and 3-15 from the tileset), decompresses the BG3 and LZ77 BG0 maps, sets the BG control registers and priorities of TransparencySetRoomEffectsTransparency, and writes the block layers' metatiles (gTilemap, then gCommonTilemap past block 1024) into the 512x256 maps around the camera. Every frame it runs AnimatedGraphicsUpdate (16 slots with their five types, mirrored at the end of VRAM for slots 12-15), the tank animation, AnimatedPaletteUpdate on palette row 15 (disabled without the alarm or the ziplines event, paused during a power bomb), the hatch flashing, and positions a liquid LZ77 BG0 from gEffectYPosition with the water wave (sWaterLoopCounterArray), which also feeds the hazard and sprite liquid surface. Lava, acid and water now animate and blend: checked by capture in norfair_022 (lava), crateria_007 (water over Samus and the Skulteras) and brinstar_000. Screen shakes (mzm_screen_shake, one shared state as gScreenShakeX/Y): a longer shake replaces the current one; once a frame a 2-pixel offset every third frame (up or left, then down or right with intensity bit 0, else nothing), halved in the last quarter second, moves BG0 to BG2 and BG3 by half, never the sprites; the room load clears them. Checked by capture during a power bomb in chozodia_005 (BG1 2 pixels left, then back). A BG_PROP_MOVING BG2 (crateria_016, kraid_030) follows ScrollBg2: BG1's position plus gBg2Movement, kept within BG2 for the GBA screen (the runtime's wider view may show past it).
next_action: Port the background effects, BG movement and haze, then compose the layers with the sprites per pixel.

title: Non-gameplay screen helpers
divergences: ProcessComplexMenuOam (rotation and scaling) is not ported yet. The screens render at the native 240x160 size, fitted to the runtime view.
notes: MzmScreen holds what the menus and cutscenes share: the GbaPpu they draw on, gOamData and gNextOamSlot, the *_NonGameplay background offsets and blending values, the EWRAM work area and gChangedInput / gButtonInput in GBA key bits. ProcessMenuOam runs the menu object animations from the ROM's struct OamArray and FrameData tables with all their pre-actions and writes the OAM parts at the object's position minus its bound background's offset, with its priority and object mode; ResetFreeOam, UpdateMenuOamDataId, ClearGfxRam and ApplySpecialBackgroundFadingColor (in, flash, out and the unnamed fade) are ported; MenuOamData records are read from their 16-byte ROM layout.
next_action: Port ProcessComplexMenuOam with the first screen that needs it.

title: GBA picture processing unit and ROM data bank
divergences: The bitmap modes 3 to 5 are not rendered; the window and blending registers are read once per frame (no mid-frame register changes or HBlank effects); the affine backgrounds use the reference point plus the line times PB/PD instead of the latched internal registers; objects beyond 128 per frame, the per-line object cycle limit and the affine object mosaic are not modelled. The ROM bank holds the whole verified ROM (private, never committed).
notes: The register bank keeps the BG2/BG3 affine range at 0x20-0x3F independent from the lower display registers; a ROM-free PPU test and the Tourian surrounded test exercise BG2PA, BG2PD, BG2X and BG2Y while DISPCNT remains live. gba_ppu renders the GBA display memories as GBATEK describes them: text backgrounds (four sizes, 16 and 256 colors, flips, scrolling, mosaic), affine backgrounds (wrap, overflow), regular and affine objects (all shapes and sizes, 1D and 2D mapping, flips, double size, semi-transparency, the object window, mosaic), the front-most two layers per pixel by priority, window 0, window 1, the object window and the outside, alpha blending, brightness up and down, and forced blank. scripts/mzm_rom_bank.py copies the verified ROM into a private bank and lists the 14462 sized data objects of the reference ELF (name, GBA address, size); mzm_rom looks them up by name and reads them by address, and decompresses the BIOS LZ77 and run-length streams.
next_action: Finish the remaining native screens and compare the affine scenes with an emulator.

title: Save file
divergences: The runtime writes its own versioned little-endian files (header, payload, CRC-32; version 2, version 1 still read) instead of the GBA SRAM layout with its copies and checksums; a file keeps the room alias, Samus's position and facing, the equipment, the events, the minimap progress, the collected items, the opened hatches, the never-reform blocks, the area, the difficulty, the in-game timer and the completed game flags, but not the music or the rest of gSamusData. gMostRecentSaveFile is the newest of the three files. The save completes in one frame instead of the multi-frame SramSaveFile stages. The difficulty is kept but its damage and drop effects are not applied (the runtime plays the normal difficulty).
notes: Three files, file_a.sav to file_c.sav in --save-dir (else SDL's preference folder). YES on a save platform's prompt writes the current file through a temporary file renamed over it. The file select screen reads their info (SramWrite_FileInfo: existence, area, energy, missiles, suit, timer, completed flags, difficulty) and continues one: its room is loaded and its state restored with Samus in SPOSE_SAVING_LOADING_GAME and gIsLoadingFile set for the room's first sprite update, so the save platform releases her; --load does the same at start with the most recent file. The in-game timer runs each game frame as InGameTimerUpdate does (frames, seconds, minutes, hours, capped at 99:59:59 with gMaxInGameTimerFlag). Truncated, corrupted, foreign or newer files are rejected. The file select screen's copy and erase menus copy a save file over another or delete it. The game over's continue loads the most recent file the same way, or restarts the game's start without one.
next_action: Port the intro, then compare the files' timer and contents with an emulator.

title: Intro
divergences: English text only: the other languages' intro text (TextStartStory) is not ported. ProcessComplexOam and CalculateOamPart4 are local copies inside the intro module (the sprite engine does not use them yet). The V-blank writes are applied right after the frame's handler, one frame earlier than on hardware. Not compared with an emulator.
notes: The runtime boots on the intro without arguments or with `--intro`, and returns to it from the file select (B) and from the game over's quit, as GM_INTRO. It runs IntroHandler frame by frame on the native screen's PPU with the ROM bank's graphics, tile tables, palettes and OAM frames: the fade from black, "EMERGENCY ORDER" typed letter by letter with its letter sounds, palette flashes and blinking marker (IntroProcessText's action tables), the ship flying towards the camera as double-size affine sprites (ProcessComplexOam, CalculateOamPart4, the intro music and ship sound), Samus in her ship with the shaking camera, "EXTERMINATE ALL METROID ORGANISMS...", the view of Zebes with the ship and its heat blended, "AND DEFEAT THE MECHANICAL LIFE-FORM, MOTHER BRAIN", Mother Brain's jar scrolling with its music, and the fuzz (the OBJ palette rewritten from scattered ROM data by IntroFuzzVBlank). It then leads to the title with its comets; A, B or START fades all sounds and the music (FadeAllSounds and FadeMusic, 10 frames) and leads to the title past its comets. The test runs the whole intro on the exported bank and checks the stage order and timings, the sounds, the letters, the affine parameters, the fuzz palette and the skip. Checked by capture: every stage, the end on the title's comets and the skip.
next_action: Compare the timing and the affine ship with an emulator, then port the game start sequence and the other cutscenes.

title: Title screen
divergences: US version only (the EU menu and languages are not ported) and no debug text. The idle demos are not ported: when TitleScreenCheckPlayEffects starts one after 17 idle seconds, the title screen is entered again past its comets, as after a demo. The V-blank writes are applied right after the frame's handler, one frame earlier than on hardware. Not compared with an emulator.
notes: The runtime boots on the intro (mzm.title.intro) without arguments or with `--intro`, and on the title screen with `--title` (Return or the gamepad's Start is START). It runs TitleScreenHandler frame by frame on the native screen's PPU: TitleScreenInit (sTitleScreenPal for BG and OBJ, the two pages of sTitleScreenPageData with their LZ77 tile tables, the title, space, decoration and sparkle graphics, the ground kept in EWRAM, the trademark symbol), the fade in from black through ApplySpecialBackgroundFadingColor, the title music (UpdateMusicPriority 2, PlayMusic MUSIC_TITLE_SCREEN), the comets view (two comets with the menu OAM animations of sTitleScreenOam, the ground scrolling in with TitleScreenTransferGroundGraphics), START skipping it (brightness down, the ground copied, brightness up), the title fading in by alpha blending, the animated palettes (sky decorations, title shine after 4 seconds, the PRESS START prompt), the two sparkles after 6 seconds, and START (the pressing sound, the fast prompt palette, the fade out). Checked by capture: the comets, the scrolled title and PRESS START, then the game after START. START now leads to the file select screen (mzm.menus.file_select), which leads back to the intro with B (GM_INTRO). After a skipped intro (gSubGameMode2 1) the title starts past its comets, as in TitleScreenInit.
next_action: Port the demos, then compare with an emulator.

title: Doors, hatches and room transitions
divergences: The mother ship hatch graphics are not reproduced; gLastDoorUsed is the arrival door of a door transition only (a loaded file or a new game locks no hatch as the one Samus came through); opened destinations are remembered by position, not by door index. Event-based area destinations (ConnectionFindEventBasedDoor) are not resolved: the normal destination is used. Door fades: the runtime's view is 320x224 with its own camera, so the door transition tilemap's tube starts at the view's edge on the door's side (its last 24 pixels shown on the right, its first 24 on the left, as on the GBA screen) and slides 336 pixels instead of 256 (56 frames instead of 43); the sprites' faded palette rows are drawn as a colour modulation of their baked frames, the BG3 blending as a black veil plus an additive layer; ColorFadingGradients' BG2/BG3 alpha steps, the haze and the window are not reproduced.
notes: Hatches are BG1 and Clipdata blocks driven by the native state machine: BgClipCheckOpeningHatch on beam, missile and laser hits (weakness and health from sHatchBehaviors, super missiles open missile hatches), the opening and closing frames of sHatchesTilemapValues with sHatchesAnimationDurationCounter, the hatch Samus comes through closing behind her, opened hatches remembered per area and overridden to normal hatches. Checked in brinstar_000: a beam opens the blue hatch through its grey frames. Hatch locks (src/runtime/mzm_hatches.c): gray hatches wait for gDoorUnlockTimer (ConnectionLoadDoors); the rooms export their sHatchLockEvents (Q lines: the hatch's door, the event, before or after, unlockable) and RoomLoad locks them as navigation hatches (ConnectionCheckHatchLockEvents); a sprite's LOCK_DOORS locks every hatch when the door fade starts (the arrival hatch closing with the locking sound), and its negative countdown unlocks them (SOUND_DOORS_UNLOCKING, the flashing hatches, then the shots open them); the Long Beam Dessgeega uses both. Door fades (src/runtime/mzm_door_fade.c): a hatch fades the room to black over 16 frames (sColorFading_345f60) except the hatches' palette row, then BG3 shows sDoorTransitionTilemap with sDoorTransitionPal, blended in over BG1 in 8 frames and covering everything (priority 0, Samus included); once the room is loaded the tube slides to the arrival door's height (3 pixels a frame), waits, slides across (6 pixels a frame), then the room comes back from black over 16 frames and the room's track starts (CheckPlayTransitionMusicTrack); the other doors fade to black over 8 frames and back. Samus waits during both (no SamusUpdate, the pause and the in-game timer wait); the medium sprites are hidden after a hatch's fade out. The backgrounds' palette fade is ApplySpecialBackgroundFadingColor on the native room palette. Checked by capture: brinstar_002's hatch to brinstar_003 and chozodia_007's passage to chozodia_037. Area connection doors (sAreaConnections: elevators and the passages between areas) now lead to the connected area's door: the exporter resolves the destination door of each, the runtime takes them like the other doors (an elevator ride without vertical offset) and RoomLoad's elevator placement follows.
next_action: Compare the door fades and the hatch locks with an emulator; port the mother ship hatches.

title: Beam and missile projectiles
divergences: The on-screen test of ProjectileCheckDespawn uses the runtime camera's top-left corner with the GBA screen size (the runtime view is wider); the missile trails' low BG priority is not drawn; projectiles without PROJ_STATUS_ABOVE_BG1 are drawn at the sprites' priority instead of one behind BG1.
notes: Power Beam, missiles and super missiles move and collide with the room; their hits on ported sprites (damage, stun, invincible hits) and their wall and sprite impact particles are ported. Missiles and super missiles drop their trails (PE_MISSILE_TRAIL every 8 frames, PE_SUPER_MISSILE_TRAIL every 4). ProjectileCheckDespawn removes beams and missiles that are both off screen (the screen plus the projectile's draw distance and two blocks of padding) and 12 blocks above or below or 10 blocks beside Samus. A missile or super missile not weak to the sprite it hits (or hitting an immune sprite) tumbles off it (ProjectileStartTumblingMissile: away from the sprite's x, its thrust sound stopped, no longer hitting sprites, drawn in front of the backgrounds) along sTumblingMissileSpeed with a pixel a frame sideways and through walls, until it leaves the screen (ProjectileMoveTumbling). Checked in brinstar_003: a missile shot diagonally at a brown Ripper bounces back and falls tumbling. (The charge and Long Beams: mzm.weapons.charge_beam; Ice: mzm.weapons.ice_beam; Wave and Plasma: mzm.weapons.wave_plasma_beams; bombs and power bombs: mzm.weapons.bombs, mzm.weapons.power_bombs). The weapon sounds play at their native points: the toggle and arming sounds of SamusSetHighlightedWeapon, the beam shot and the missile and super missile shot and thrust on ProjectileInit, the thrust stopped by the impact particles.
next_action: Add the missile and beam item pickups with the item sprites.

title: Bombs, bomb jumps and bomb damage
divergences: Liquids (no bounce when slowed) are not ported;
notes: With the Bombs item, B in the Morph Ball places a bomb (four at most, 7 frames apart) at Samus's position: a slow then a fast spin of 16 frames each with their native sprites, then the PE_BOMB explosion and 16 frames during which CAA_BOMB_PISTOL reaches nine points, one a frame (bomb blocks, bomb chains, hatches). On the first explosion frame Samus bounces off a touching bomb (up, left or right from the bomb's middle and gPreviousXPosition; only falling and from below when airborne), and the explosion damages sprites weak to beams and bombs (8). The set and explosion sounds play. Checked in brinstar_000: the bounce, then the three bomb blocks under Samus break. A bomb taken by a morph ball launcher spins again (16 + 16 frames), then its explosion affects no block but launches Samus in morph ball touching it (forcedMovement FORCED_MOVEMENT_LAUNCHED_BY_CANNON, SPOSE_DELAY_BEFORE_BALLSPARKING). The runtime runs ProjectileCheckHittingSprite where ProjectileUpdate does, after the new projectile's spawn and before the projectile loop (MzmWeapons.hit_sprites), so the explosion's PROJ_STATUS_CAN_AFFECT_ENVIRONMENT, set when the fast spin ends, is taken by the next update's pass once.
next_action: Port the bomb behaviour in liquids.

title: Charge Beam, Long Beam and the pseudo screw
divergences: The pseudo screw's Samus effect is not drawn.
notes: With the Charge Beam, holding B with no weapon armed counts the charge to 79, then back to 64; releasing it fires a charged beam from 64 or a normal beam above 25; the B press itself still fires a beam, arming a weapon drops the charge and the Morph Ball releases a full charge as it forms or rolls. The charging particle starts at 16 with the begin-to-charge sound (stopped when the charge drops), turns charged at 64 with the full-charge loop every 16 frames, follows the arm cannon and hides in the spin poses; Samus uses the charging palette rows (two consecutive rows by 16-frame step, none on the fourth) and the beam release rows. The Long Beam moves 24 subpixels a frame without the short lifetime, with its hit damage (3) and impact; the charged beams (two at a time, hitboxes 12 and 16, damage 8 and 12) hit sprites weak to the charge beam or beams. Beam shots set the ProjectileSetBeamParticleEffect flash at the cannon. A full charge during a spin is the pseudo screw: 4 * (2 + beams) to weak sprites, PSEUDO_SCREW_DESTROYED on a kill, Samus still hurt by survivors. The beam particles are exported per loaded beam variant (graphics set and sBeamPal row) in the projectile library. Checked in tourian_010: the charge glow and palette, then the charged Long Beam and its flash. The charged Long Beam drops PE_CHARGED_LONG_BEAM_TRAIL every 8 frames.
next_action: Add the beam item pickups with the item sprites.

title: Ice Beam and freezing
divergences: the trails' low BG priority is not drawn; frozenPaletteRowOffset is taken as 0 for every sprite.
notes: The Ice Beam (over the Long Beam) moves 26 subpixels a frame and drops a trailing particle half a block from it when gFrameCounter8Bit & 3 is 0 (drifting one subpixel sideways and one pixel down a frame); its shot, charge and impact sounds, beam graphics, sBeamPal row 2, release row 2 and charging rows 4 and 5 are used. Hits: a sprite weak to beams freezes for 240 when freezable and frame8 & its freeze flag (metadata high byte) is 0, taking 3 (4 with Long Beam) as ice damage; otherwise normal damage; freezable but immune sprites freeze with no damage; others take the solid hit. The charged Ice Beam (12, 16 with Long Beam) needs a charge-beam or beam weakness and always freezes freezable sprites. Freezing sets the frozen row (15 - graphics slot), plays SOUND_FREEZING_SPRITE and the freezing particle (drawn every other frame); every ported AI then only counts the timer down every other frame and flickers in its last 45 ticks. The stun timer now flashes the stun row (14 - slot). The exporter bakes /frozen and /stun variants of every sprite frame. Pseudo screw damage counts the Ice Beam. Checked in brinstar_003 (`--item ice-beam`, L held, B taps): a brown Ripper freezes blue under the ice impact and freezing particles, trails follow the shots and Samus flashes the ice release row. Frozen sprites are solid: a falling Samus lands on them (SpriteUtilSamusStandingOnSprite, STANDING_ENEMY), rising into one stops her under it and walking into one stops her at its side; its kill drops her. Checked in ridley_003 (`--item ice-beam --item charge-beam`): a charged shot freezes a Dessgeega, Samus jumps onto it and stands there until it thaws, then takes its contact damage. The charged Ice Beam also drops PE_CHARGED_ICE_BEAM_TRAIL every 8 frames. A frozen sprite touching Samus on a zipline drops her (SpriteUtilCheckOnZipline: SPOSE_MID_AIR_REQUEST). The paralyzer pistol applies the native suitless Space Pirate freeze countdown and black/purple flicker.
next_action: Compare the freezing and thaw timing with an emulator.

title: Suitless paralyzer pistol
divergences: The charged pistol trail is drawn at the normal particle priority instead of its native low BG priority; no direct Chozodia capture is recorded yet.
notes: Suitless Samus automatically charges the pistol every frame: B fires the harmless normal shot before 112 frames or the charged shot from 112 through the 127-to-112 wrap, with the native two/six projectile limits, seven-frame cooldown and shot sounds. Both shots use CAA_BOMB_PISTOL, travel 22 subpixels per moving frame without the short-beam lifetime and use their native directional OAM and hitboxes; the charged shot drops PE_CHARGED_PISTOL_TRAIL every eight frames. The normal shot always produces an invincible hit. The charged shot deals 12 to sprites weak to charge shots or beams, but a Space Pirate is instead paralysed for 60 ticks with the suitless black/purple flicker and no damage. The projectile exporter stages the pistol graphics and palette for its muzzle flash and charged trail.
next_action: Port the suitless item-acquisition map sequence, then validate the weapon in Chozodia against an emulator.

title: Power bombs and their explosion
divergences: The explosion's look is an approximation drawn over the background layers behind the sprites (the yellow tint and the BLDY 12 darkening outside the native window rows; the layers in front of the sprites are not darkened), not the native palette and blending registers; PowerBombExplosionEnd's blend fade takes one frame; the native GET_CLIP_BLOCK reads past the room's right edge, the port skips those blocks.
notes: In the Morph Ball, R arms power bombs (with ammunition); B (the Bombs item is required, as natively) places one, at most one at a time and none during an explosion: one ammunition (the last disarms them), a slow spin of 54 frames and a fast one of 40, then PowerBombExplosionStart. The semi-minor axis grows by 3 a frame to 159, holds five frames, shrinks back to 4 and ends; while expanding, CAA_POWER_BOMB reaches the hitbox's left and right block columns (even frames) or top and bottom rows (odd frames) from the centre outward, opening power bomb hatches and breaking blocks; every sprite touching the hitbox takes 50 (weak) once per power bomb. The set and explosion sounds play; power bomb drops spawn and refill one. The window rows come from sHaze_PowerBomb_WindowValuesPointers (power_bomb.tsv). Checked in brinstar_000: the explosion and the bomb blocks it breaks. The explosion starts a two-second horizontal screen shake (one way only, intensity 0x80).

title: Wave and Plasma Beams
divergences: The ice-coloured Wave and Plasma projectiles are pre-rendered with sBeamPal row 2 over their graphics set (the /ice library keys); the projectiles' draw order follows PROJ_STATUS_ABOVE_BG1 only (in front of every background, or at the sprites' priority); no item pickup gives the beams yet (debug menu and --item only).
notes: SamusCheckNewProjectile picks plasma, then wave, ice, long for the beam type and the matching shot sound (all 24 normal and charged combinations); the charge sounds and the release (rows 3 and 4) and charging rows (6 and 8) follow ParticlePlayBeginToChargeSound and SamusUpdatePalette. The Wave Beam moves 28 subpixels a frame through walls, applying CAA_BEAM to three points across the wave (one block away, 45 subpixels diagonally) every frame; the Plasma Beam moves 32 and stops at walls (its impact) unless the Wave Beam is equipped, and goes through the sprites it hits. Both drop the ice trail with the Ice Beam; the charged ones drop their trails (wave, plasma, or the full beam trail with Plasma and Wave) every 8 frames. Their hitboxes are the native per-direction boxes (wave, charged wave and their Plasma variants, with the float factors truncated). Hits deal 3 plus one per other beam (charged 12 plus four) with the Wave or Plasma impact, or are ice hits with the full beam particles when the Ice Beam is equipped. The projectile library exports the Wave and Plasma tables, their ice-coloured versions, the new impact and trail particles for each loaded beam variant (the Plasma trails only with the Plasma graphics). Checked in brinstar_003 (`--item wave-beam --item long-beam`): a wave shot crosses the right wall and stays drawn in front of it until it leaves the screen; with `--item plasma-beam` the green shot goes through a Ripper.
